==English==

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*weh₁-|*dʰeh₁-}}
From {{der|en|fro|verifier}} (French: {{m|fr|vérifier}}), from {{der|en|la-med|-}} {{m|la|vērificō|vērificāre|t=make true}}, from {{der|en|la|vērus||true}} + {{m|la|faciō||do, make}}; see [[-fy]].

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈvɛɹɪfaɪ/}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-verify.wav|a=Southern England}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[substantiate]] or [[prove]] the [[truth]] of something.
#* {{RQ:Bramah Eyes of Max Carrados|passage="It is early to judge," he remarked, after stopping the car in order to '''verify''' the name on the brass plate, "but, upon my word, Max, I really think that our ghost might have discovered more appropriate quarters."}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[confirm]] or [[test]] the truth or [[accuracy]] of something.
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1984|journal=InfoWorld|volume=6|issue=14|page=67
|passage=In comparison, it takes about a minute to save, rewind and manually '''verify''' a similar file on a cassette.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|legal}} To [[affirm]] something [[formally]], under [[oath]].
